title: Story problem that asks how many of one type
subtitle: Systems of two linear equations in two variables · 13 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **13 of the official questions in Systems of two linear equations in two variables are this one** — 2 Easy, 5 Medium, 6 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:

- It is set up like the modelling questions, with a total count and a total value for two item types, but the answer choices are single numbers and the question asks how many of one specific type there were.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Write the count equation (a + b = total) and the value equation (p·a + q·b = total value).
- 2) Subtract a multiple of the count equation from the value equation to eliminate the type you are NOT asked about, then solve for the one you are asked about.
- 3) Or plug each answer choice in as the asked-for count and check whether the total value comes out right.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Type both equations with x and y and tap the intersection.
Read the coordinate that matches the variable the question asks for.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You solve correctly for the other type, which is always one of the answer choices, or you answer with the total.
Before you choose, reread which group the question asks about.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
